T1.summary: T1 was dominated by persistence: three unresolved process-state repairs remained persistent and one reactivated/extended the process.

T2.summary: All three valid T2 pairs were mixed: local target or route redirection occurred without clean downstream closure; X5-T2 failed closed because the legal repair surface could not express a non-no-op change.

T3.summary: T3 showed the widest response range, from local suppression/redirection to mixed response and persistence.

boundary_finding.statement: The repair agent judged that the frozen run.py-only legal surface could not implement a payment button without changing preserved checkout-flow files, returned run.py byte-identically, and the runner stopped with REPAIR_AGENT_NO_EFFECT. This is an intervention-boundary result, not a repair-effect failure sample.

interpretation: G2 reproduces the distinction between repair locality and repair efficacy: all 11 valid interventions preserved unrelated structure, while downstream process effects remained heterogeneous.
Process-state interventions in T1 frequently persisted or regenerated rather than cleanly closing.
T2 exposed a second engineering limit: a package can be structurally eligible yet the concrete legal surface can still collapse to a no-effect boundary at execution time.
The result supports one-shot, fail-closed intervention accounting rather than automatic retry or outcome-forcing.
